keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 23-36; no Cliopatria row (its Xin shape ends in 23, ea-02-c). The Hexi Corridor page: it 'came under the control of warlord Dou Rong' after the Xin collapse of 23, settled by large numbers of Qiang; the Guangwu page: 'western Gansu and northern Qinghai region, west of the Yellow River'. The page speaks of four Hexi commanderies; no frontier is given.

ledger.note: 23: Dou Rong holds the Hexi Corridor. 'The Hexi Corridor was settled by large numbers of Qiang people and came under the control of warlord Dou Rong' after the Xin collapse in 23 CE; a footnote has him 'from A.D. 24 onward warlord of the Kansu corridor'.

region.text: Dou Rong: 'independently controlled the modern western Gansu and northern Qinghai region, west of the Yellow River'

ledger.note: 36: Hexi is handed over. 'After Chengjia's fall, Dou turned over the lands under his control to Emperor Guangwu in AD 36, and was made prime controller.' The Hexi Corridor page dates his submission to the reinstated Eastern Han to 29: Hexi was probably a Han client between 29 and 36, but no page says so.

region.text: Dou Rong: 'independently controlled the modern western Gansu and northern Qinghai region, west of the Yellow River'

ledger.note: 36: Dou Rong's Hexi ends in the Eastern Han's unification (25 December 36 for China proper, Guangwu footnote).

certainty.note: Only the modern region is named; the Hexi page gives four commanderies.

sources.note: The rival regional powers of AD 25-36: who controlled which modern region; dates of their fall.

notes: Dou Rong, Hexi 23-36. 2 pages opened (Emperor Guangwu of Han; Hexi Corridor); no English article of his own (the first fetch of 'Dou Rong' returned URL_NOT_FOUND), no Cliopatria row. The pages disagree: the Hexi page has his submission in 29 and his start in 23 (24 in a footnote), the Guangwu page has the handover of his lands in 36. 36 is used for the end, as in ea-02-c's han-dynasty dossier; a Han vassal tie 29-36 is plausible (ea-02-c or a gap-filler may add vassal events). The Hexi page names no Dou Rong capital. Counterparts: han-dynasty and xin-dynasty exist.
